description: We are Beyond Gravity, a team passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. Our goal is to develop creative solutions to real-world challenges using NASA data. We welcome motivated people interested in programming, AI, data analysis, scientific research, UI/UX design, and presentations. You don’t need to be an expert. We value teamwork, creativity, curiosity, and a willingness.
summary: NASA DECODED is an interactive e-book that introduces school-age learners to spacecraft engineering through original NASA mission records. Developed for the NASA Space Apps challenge Abandoned but Not Forgotten, it tells the stories of three pieces of hardware still beyond Earth: the Opportunity rover, the descent stage of Apollo 11’s lunar module Eagle, and the Voyager Golden Record. Each chapter opens with a story told from the hardware’s point of view and gives learners a question to investigate.On Mars, learners use Opportunity’s detection of hematite to explore evidence of past water in Water Detective. On the Moon, they use Apollo 11 records and an orbital image to distinguish the stage that stayed on the surface from the one that carried the crew back to lunar orbit. In deep space, they use NASA’s catalog to decide what belongs on the Golden Record.Character videos, illustrated logbooks with optional read-aloud, and interactive diagrams help learners explore each mission at their own pace. Ask Nova offers mission-specific hints, while games and a final quiz give learners a chance to apply what they’ve learned. The goal is for learners to explain what each piece of hardware did and identify the evidence behind their answer.
details:
How it works

·        Choose a mission: The map opens Opportunity’s chapter first. Learners can watch the character video, read or listen to the logbook, and tap numbered markers to see the function of each spacecraft part.

·        Inspect the evidence: In Science discovery, the Real NASA Mission Evidence section links to original images, instrument measurements, and mission records. It also collects updates related to each mission.

·        Use what you learned: Learners play Water Detective, match Eagle’s parts to their jobs, and select items for the Golden Record. Each game gives immediate feedback. Completing all three missions unlocks the final quiz and a personalized Space Explorer certificate that learners can save or print.

·        Get help from Ask Nova: The in-book chatbot follows the current mission. Learners can choose a topic, type a question, ask for hints that become more specific, or hear a reply read aloud. A separate eight-question practice quiz gives immediate feedback.

Key benefits and intended impact

In our exploratory survey of 40 parents, 23 (57.5%) selected YouTube or other video platforms as their child’s main source for learning about space outside school. Another result was that 21 (52.5%) cited too few chances to interact or practice. These responses guided our decision to pair short videos with hands-on activities. In a future learner test, we would ask children to explain a mission clue in their own words.

Survey Results:https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G8lzzZEuit1Qt8vim93Byel2rmPg-cY0/view?usp=sharing

Interface and creative choices

·        Large buttons and clear labels: The mission map and chapter menus make it easy to see what can be tapped. Labels such as My logbook and Science discovery tell learners what each choice opens.

·        Distinct colors for different actions: Color helps learners distinguish the reading, discovery, and game options. The labels explain each action in words.

·        Expressive voices and optional read-aloud: Taking inspiration from family animation, we chose friendly voices to make the spacecraft characters approachable. Learners can hear the characters speak or follow the written story at their own pace.

Tools, technologies, and team roles

The e-book uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and is hosted on Netlify. Nour led the parent survey and analysis, edited the project videos, and prepared the demonstration slides. Abdullah led web development and character media production. Both researched the missions and designed the learning activities.

·        Character media and scripting. Google Flow generated character artwork, animation, and dialogue. Gemini helped refine prompts. ChatGPT supported scripts, storyboards, shot planning, and video prototypes, and generated 3D props and transition sounds for the deck. Codex assisted with the e-book code.

·        ChatGPT-connected video workflow. We connected Descript while exploring editing options. Nour manually assembled and refined the final videos in CapCut.

·        Ask Nova in the published e-book. The chatbot matches questions to prepared responses and runs in the browser. Read-aloud uses browser speech synthesis. The project includes an optional Netlify function for OpenAI-generated replies.
